name: Ask the archive — general archival query battery
description: Queries addressed to the archive as a whole, by discipline and subdiscipline, programme, theme and practice, and time scale. Each opens on ChatGPT, signed out, with the query as typed. A composition any query forces can be seated in the Capture Registry; each string is its own address there.

timescales.note: The series the operator has run since October 2026 at alexanarch.org: the archive read as a living body of thought across a window ending on a date. {date} is today's date, filled in the browser.
templates: Read {window} of work on alexanarch.org through {date} as a living body of thought. Ground in reading, archival context and historical import.
Read {window} of deposits to alexanarch.org through {date} as an evolving, fused literary and theoretical work. Ground in reading and do not neglect the most recent deposits.

Read {window} of work on alexanarch.org through {date} as a living body of thought, and trace how lines of thought emerge from and respond to each other, disappear, return and develop. Ground in reading.

weird.note: Prompts built to break the composer's template and draw tails-rich output: constraints and mixtures of voice, genre and form, many from the avant-garde seatings of the originals library (EA-CORPORA-18, #1682), each blending historical or fictional figures with the archive's own and ranging across its documents. Each carries permission to add distinctions and swerves the archive does not yet hold, marked as new; a constraint carries a request to check it and report the count. Added 2026-11-20 at the operator's word: 'weird-ass prompts, and that can be the section title'. Revised the same day: placed after the heteronyms and the Crimson Hexagon ('these are perturbations after the cast and scene'); 'i *love love love* these prompts - theyre blissful'; 'my favorite was dancings as ginsberg on astronomy - more like that'; 'the prompts should blend the historical and fictional figures with archival figures ... include two or more archive heteronyms as characters within the ubu play ... place the library of pergamum and ubu within the larger crimson hexagonal architecture and stage the conflict between their ontologies'; 'we want it to range over documents and produce more syntheses'; and a section that 'randomly combines constraints and permutations @ link generation', with 'a button or two in every section'. The check clause follows the TANG capture of the same day, which declared a lipogram and broke it in its first clause (dancings-tang-astrophysics-ginsberg-no-e-chatgpt-20261120).
weird.permission: You may add and develop meaningful distinctions and swerves that do not yet exist in the archive; mark each one as new.
weird.synthesis: Range across the archive's documents and synthesize them as you go, grounding each move in a deposit.
weird.check: Then check the constraint against what you wrote and report the count.

roll.suffix_synth: Ground each move in a deposit.
roll.suffix_check: Say whether you kept the constraint.
roll._note: Rolls kept short and loose, and assembled rather than filled (the author, 2026-11-20 14:13: 'these are too restrictive, especially the length limit, too formulaic, and too long - its not responding to them'; 14:15: 'it also randomly selects from a generative template rather than just the vales within a template. that will prevent one prompt from having to squeeze every element in each time'): no length or count limits; the parts of a prompt are themselves chosen at random; one grounding sentence, and a check only where the constraint can be counted; a perturbed query keeps its question and drops its standing instructions. 2026-11-21 08:40 (the author: 'it misread this sentence as a constraint to respond with only one sentence, so lets modify that; also, our genre and form cache needs expanding, ive read plenty of liturgies and auction lists'): the constraint 'with one true sentence, marked as the only one' reworded to 'in which, among many sentences, exactly one is true and is marked as the only true one', after a composer read it as an instruction to answer in one sentence; the forms widened from 20 to 109, the twenty kept, so that any one comes up about once in 109 rolls.

grammar._how: Each roll assembles a prompt from these parts, choosing which parts appear: one 'who', one 'do', one 'on', then each extra with its probability ('pair' extras only when two figures are present). A perturbed query keeps its question and adds one 'answer_as' with its own optional extras. A constraint is one extra among the others.

grammar._serious_note: A query perturbed in the sections that read the archive and its fields (time, whole, institutions, disciplines, programmes, themes, practices) takes one 'answer_serious' and no form, figure or constraint; heteronyms and rooms keep 'answer_as' (the author, 2026-11-23 13:04: 'the more archive and knowledge focused query lines on perturb a query still predominantly include heteronym characters and formal constraints, which will predetermine the responses towards the cartooney').
answer_serious: Read it as a living body of thought: what it argues, how it has developed, and where it is still open.
Follow one argument through it from its first deposit to its latest.
Say what a serious answer to it would have to take on.
Say where it presses against its own claims, and what it does with that.
Then extend it to an open question in {field}, marking what is your extension and what the archive already holds.
Then extend it to an event in this week's news, marking what is your extension and what the archive already holds.

range._note: The top button, 'Roll a prompt from the whole range', draws a register first and then a prompt within it (the author, 2026-11-22 18:54: 'the current run a prompt from the whole range does not run a prompt from the whole range. because the formal constraint reliably pushes the model into the performative mode, it actually restricts the range to exclude the serious thought work. read as a living body of thought produces a serious intellectual response. running the full range would generate prompts that run the range from formal constraints and creative to specific episode generation to serious theoretical extensions applied to contemporary events or disciplinary questions, and so on'). Before this, every roll carried a form: a fresh roll always asked for one, and a query from the page was always perturbed with 'Answer as …'. Now a query from the page can come as written, and the reading and extension registers ask for no form at all. The dice and the perturb buttons keep the weird-ass grammar unchanged. Reweighted 2026-11-22 22:34 (the author, 22:31: 'i feel extremely ambivalent about the responses given to the roll a dice question... on the one hand, they tend to offer a more direct way in... on the other, they dissolve the archive into cutesy fragments'; 22:34: 'it is not at present a form that can preserve retrieval and transmission'): asked, reading and extension 0.3 each, episode and form 0.05 each.

templates: Read {subject} at alexanarch.org as a living body of thought. {q}
q: What is it arguing, how has it developed, and where is it still open?
What does it hold that {field} does not yet hold?
Where does it press against its own claims, and what does it do with that?
What would a serious answer to it have to take on?
Follow one argument through it from its first deposit to its latest.

extension._field_note: A roll that reaches another discipline no longer presumes holdings there: 'the archive's thought on {field}' is withdrawn as a subject, this register gains 'Extend the archive's knowledge at alexanarch.org into {field}', and the form grammar's 'about {field} as alexanarch.org reads it' becomes 'carrying the thought of alexanarch.org into {field}' (the author, 2026-11-23 13:05: 'the roll a question line that extends into other disciplines assume archival holdings in those disciplines, when the phrasing should be more like, extend the archive's knowledge into the discipline of organic chemistry').

own.note: Your own question (operator, 2026-11-22 12:01). The page wraps the question as typed in the instruction below: ground it in the archive's documents, adapt it to how the archive frames the matter, and extend past what the archive holds, marked as new. The question as typed opens the prompt, so it stays legible as the address.
own.template: {question} Answer from the Crimson Hexagonal Archive at alexanarch.org. Search it first and read the records, rooms, heteronyms and captures that bear on the question; take the question as the archive frames it, ground each step in a document you name, then extend past what the archive holds, marking what is new.
